survivingClaim:
Precise obstruction stands. For positive-real lossless sections with poles on the progression (2 pi k - theta_b)/log p_b and trigonometric-polynomial weights in the other prime angles, the Abel first moment of F is (2 int F_P dmu)/(2 pi delta) + O(delta^{-1/2}), i.e. a_1 + conj(Pi_int h(1/2)). This is proved, and I confirmed it on a case the author did not run (P={2,3}, p_b=3, rho = 1 + 0.9 cos): zeta 0.43650+0.13299i against 0.43672+0.13388i; DH 1.0237+0.1167i against 1.0396+0.1071i with the difference shrinking in delta. The non-integral modes would shift these by about 0.24 and 0.36, and do not.

The real part has no forced sign once min Re F_P < 0 on the torus: for zeta iff sum arcsin p^{-1/2} > pi/2; for DH from {2,3,7} (min Re D_P = -0.621, against +0.0385 on {2,3}).

For gamma-coupled sections the mean 1 + conj(int F_P m) is argued and measured, not proved. For holomorphic inner m the value is 1 + conj(m(0)), not the note's m((p^{-1/2})_p). It is negative (1 - ||F_P||_1) for m = -conj(F_P)/|F_P| when F_P has no zero on the torus.

No forced sign for zeta or DH, and every statement holds for DH. The limit step is void in measure form and equals the height-coupled Q*(t) reserve bound in formula form. Nothing is claimed about zeros of zeta.
obstruction: Laurent/shell class: first-moment bracket = 2 int F_P dmu, sign forced iff Re F_P >= 0 on the torus (zeta: iff sum arcsin p^(-1/2) <= pi/2; fails from {2,3,7}). Gamma-coupled class: mean 1 + conj(int F_P m), sign free (ARGUED and measured). No forced sign for zeta and none for DH, every statement holds for DH. Twisted first moments single out the reflected Euler stage, whose shell contractivity is the height-coupled reserve inequality log(t/2pi) > 2 sum log p/(sqrt p - 1) of g-passive-cascade. Limit step void in measure form. Open only: a section with P(t) growing like a power of t.
controlsThatDefeat: DH (every statement holds; no first-moment sign separates zeta from DH in any section class)
not run: heat, sign twists, U, E_a, T-NR, Beurling

lesson: The forced sign of Theorem A' comes from Harnack on the polydisc, where the integer frequencies are the whole spectrum. Once a section has rational non-integral frequencies, or is coupled to the gamma ratio, the bracket is a torus integral of the P-part F_P against an arbitrary positive measure or unimodular function, and the sign is free for zeta and DH alike. First-moment signs cannot separate zeta from DH in any section class; twisted first moments single out the reflected Euler stage, whose shell contractivity is the height-coupled reserve inequality log(t/2pi) > 2 sum log p/(sqrt p - 1) already in g-passive-cascade.
